activity.name: Bash
activity.arg:
git status --short | head -8; git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
c0014: the block row says which block it is, and stops offering an empty one

A swatch is a colour with a format letter on it, and neither of those says what
the block *is*. The behaviour and trigger rows carry their words beside them;
the block row could not, because five swatches share 324 pixels and "Obstacle,
never breaks" is 195 of them. So the words go where there is already room for
them: the "BLOCK" heading gives up its right-hand end to the name of whichever
block the brush is set to. The names are what tells the five apart in play,
which is how much it takes to break them - `block_spawn` gives `Simple` one hit
point, `Hardling` two, `Concrete` three, `SimpleTop` one but only from above,
and an `Obstacle` is not `Hittable` at all.

It is a `ChosenBlock` item rather than an `Entry`, so `palette_items` stays a
pure layout function that knows nothing about the brush - the drawing reads it,
as it already did for the `Brush   AA` row at the top - and a click on the name
chooses nothing, because it says what is chosen rather than offering something
to choose.

The sixth swatch is gone, and with it `PaletteEntry::Block`'s `Option`. `.` in
the token's first character is how a *file* says a cell is empty; it is not a
block anybody paints, so the type no longer has a way to say it. The trigger's
`Option` stays - `.` in the third character is a real thing to paint, a block in
no trigger at all - and so does `Brush::erase`, which is what `Brush::erasing()`
is. The right mouse button is now the only thing that picks one up, which it
already was in practice; the four doc comments calling it a stopgap until the
palette could switch the brush's own erase mode on are no longer true.

Five new tests, 278 green. Three pure - every block type having a name and no
two sharing one, the heading keeping room beside it for a name a click does not
land on, and nothing in the whole palette painting an empty cell. Two drive a
real app: the name on screen following the chosen block through all five and
saying only that one, and the block row being five swatches with the right
button still clearing a cell. Three mutations checked to fail: a block type with
no name, the heading naming a fixed block rather than the chosen one, and
choosing a block putting the erase brush down.

Checked in the running game, because whether the name fits is the one thing a
headless test cannot answer: with the brush on `ZA`, "Obstacle, never breaks"
lays out at 194x18 inside its 236x26 node and "BLOCK" at 61x18 inside 84x26 -
one line each, 42 pixels of slack on the longest name there is - and the row
drew five swatches and no sixth.
